patients.label: 57-year-old man with pulmonary and cutaneous Nocardia mexicana infection
attribution_limitations: The abstract says the patient was diagnosed as having tuberculosis at first, while the case text says tuberculosis was suspected; neither text says the diagnosis was formally ruled out, only that M. tuberculosis PCR on BAL was negative.
The wording "the patient was not treated after 2 weeks" is unclear; the source does not say what treatment failed or whether the anti-tuberculosis drugs were continued.

The source does not state whether the single isolate DSH41 used for phenotypic tests, susceptibility testing and 16S rRNA sequencing came from BAL or the wound; separate lines say N. mexicana was isolated from both.
The abstract and results use plural wording ("first cases", "patients") although only one patient is described.
Dissemination is stated only as a possibility ("could be disseminated", "supposed"); brain CT and blood culture were reported normal and negative and no disseminated site is documented.
